answer: The forge multiplier is published, charged in tundra, and umber lists each payment. The admission burn is multiplied by 20 for each member already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival burns the most. A burst of registrations hence prices itself out, since the marginal alias burns more than the first by design. A farm of 4730 identities would post 1429 proofs and burn roughly 51 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is an escrow account with a referee holding the key: both sides can claim anything, and only the deposit settles the argument.
